question.text: Priya manages an AIF and also personally wants to invest in a company where her fund is investing. This is:

answer.text: A potential conflict of interest that must be disclosed and managed per the fund's conflict of interest policy
Only allowed if the investment is less than INR 1 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook notes that the Manager or Sponsor may co-invest in investee companies where the AIF invests (pp.59 and 87-88) and that any such conflicts must be disclosed and mitigated through written conflict-of-interest policies and disclosures (pp.153 and 169). Priya's personal investment alongside her fund therefore falls in the "potential conflict — disclose and manage" category, not in an "automatic permission" or "blanket prohibition" bucket. The Trap: It is not automatically permitted without disclosure, not prohibited in all circumstances, and is not gated by an arbitrary rupee threshold. The governing requirements are disclosure and management under the fund's conflict-of-interest policy. Note: Source references: NISM Series XIX-A workbook pp.59 and 87-88 (manager/sponsor co-investment with the AIF) and pp.153 and 169 (conflicts to be disclosed and mitigated through written policies).
